rationale: Factor(A,r) is the exact entrywise nonnegative real Gram factor with r finite columns. This is complete positivity itself and does not confuse CP with doubly nonnegative matrices.

The upper assertion uses width exactly 9 with zero-column padding, which is equivalent to at most 9. It quantifies over every real order-six CP matrix, including singular and zero-entry matrices and A=0.
The lower conjunct retains the displayed maximum-equals-nine target: one CP matrix has no factor at any natural width r<9. Together with the upper conjunct this is exactly cp-rank 9 for that witness.
The empty width-zero factor correctly represents the zero matrix. There is no silent default rank for non-CP matrices and no positive-definite, support-pattern or boundary restriction on the domain.
The complete canonical README and ORIGINAL.md agree byte for byte. The specification distinguishes the original statement from stronger witness properties in the resolution.
